notes.title: A sequel to Supermarket - Before Exit: Gas Station Arrives 10.10.2025
notes.content:
Hello everyone,
While we are 100% focused on polishing our product we have some exciting news to share - Before Exit: Gas Station now has an official release date!


The full version of the game will launch on October 10th, 2025. 🎉 
To mark this milestone, we’ve prepared a brand-new trailer that not only announces the release date but also gives you a fresh look at what’s coming.
[previewyoutube="tJCa-Mg5D30;full"][/previewyoutube]
It's fully based on in-game gameplay and should give you more insight of what is coming besides just closing the station...

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45055880/6e6da3ef8a2de47c04d3ebcfba6bfd8792a25057.png"]
Playtests continues!


At the same time, our playtests are still ongoing. We’re carefully reviewing all of the feedback you’ve been sending us, and it’s been incredibly helpful in shaping the game. If you haven’t had a chance to participate yet, it’s not too late - the playtest is still open, and you can join directly from our Steam page.

We also want to take a moment to say thank you to everyone who has already taken part. Your insights, ideas, and time mean a lot to us. We can’t wait to share some of the results of this collaboration with the whole community in the near future.

This is a huge step forward for Before Exit: Gas Station, and we’re thrilled to finally be able to set our sights on the release. The journey continues - and we’re glad to have you with us!


See you everyone on 10.10! Thanks!

notes.title: Before Exit Gas Station is shaping up! Wishlist now!🚪
notes.content:
Hey everyone! 👋

We’re super excited to share with you progres regards Before Exit: Gas Station ⛽✨

https://i.imgur.com/uH6j49V.gif

If you played (and hopefully enjoyed 😉) our first game, you’ll be happy to know your beloved employee is back, this time working the late shift at a lonely little gas station. Your mission? Close everything down for the night. That means sweeping floors, cleaning toilets, restocking shelves, double-checking the workshop, shutting off the fuel dispensers… basically making sure everything is in order before heading home. Sounds simple, right? Well, not if your boss has anything to say about it - he notices every little mistake, and you’re already this close to getting fired…

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42863686/c14cd69b99bbabf89daf022e7463c8de87844b72.png

Like the first game, this one mixes roguelike elements, puzzles, and a chill walking-sim vibe. And for the first time in the series, you can actually step outside your workplace before calling it a day! 🌙

We’re working hard to bring you that same cozy-yet-tense feeling of the original, but with a fresh twist. And here’s a little teaser for the future: we’re developing a multiplayer mode so you can (maybe) survive those closing shifts together! More on that soon 👀


👉 If this sounds like your kind of night shift adventure, it would mean the world to us if you add Before Exit: Gas Station to your Steam Wishlist. It really helps us out and keeps you in the loop for updates!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3268520/Before_Exit_Gas_Station/

Thanks for all your love and support - you’re the reason we’re able to keep making these quirky little games. 💛

Stay tuned, and don’t forget to turn off the lights before you leave 😉

notes.title: Devlog #11 - Release date annoucement!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

08.08.2024

Yes, release of Before Exit on PC is less than month away. We basically completed whole gameplay loop and now we are focusing on polishing and fixing issues that we have found. We have playtested the game and even in current state it was pretty playable, so we expect that release should go expected to proceed smoothly…

… as always.

We are not experienced studio, but we already went trough some game releases. Some of them was directly produced by us, in some we were part of a team. It’s hard to predict what will exactly happen after such crucial day in a game development cycle. Will there be game breaking bug that we have to patch right after? Or some players will experience crashes that we never encounter? Or there will be silence and no one buys our game? 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45055880/e6195bcd00ebac97d9cc4cd1fe50b66363244857.png

No matter what, we will have our latest answer in less than a month. We hope you all hop on this train and help us make Before Exit the best possible experience!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45055880/d8ec7ceea35d19c98d731fcf81677286ace8f05e.jpg

Again, we warmly invite you to visit our Discord and add the game to your wish list!

notes.content:
Hello Customers!

We are still working hard, buuut what would a day be without a decent devlog? Today I want to introduce you to my new friend - Crate cart! 

https://i.imgur.com/ni5jY6X.jpeg
It helps with the distribution of crates around the storage and shop. The player can carry crates by hand, but it is less time-efficient and he can grab only one per run…

https://i.imgur.com/7DXfzr7.gif

…because a cart can carry two crates simultaneously! 

https://i.imgur.com/bGG6mGP.gif
It uses the same driving system as our shopping cart, and it is still bugged a little bit but still, you will be able to move crates faster! We will use it in certain scenarios where the player will be asked to move some crates around the shop. It is only for the player to decide what tool he will use, but he has to be fast and careful, not to be fired at the end of the shift!

https://i.imgur.com/ENSbfDZ.jpeg

Still, there is work to be done and it can be buggy sometimes, but those issues will be fixed in no time!

Additionally, We have recently updated our logo with subtitles! On this opportunity, take a look at what the logo design looked like from which we chose the best one:

notes.title: Devlog #9 - “Dear Diary, he didn’t fire me today…
notes.content:
Customers!

We are making progress with the gameplay scenarios that you will encounter in the game. We don’t want to spoil anything, but there are first indicators about your cause in this shop! 

https://i.imgur.com/dgtZ4q3.jpeg
(those one in Polish, we didn't have translations yet. Sorry!)

Of course, those are not your only sources about what to do in the game, but a large part of the tasks will require that you deduce them from the environment or guess them based on the right setting. 

The first note is a static objective list, it tells you what you should check first if you want to complete each evening. This note is more of a signpost than a checklist, there will be things to do that are not noted there - but that is exactly what makes our game fun!

The second list gives you insight into your progress - you will get fired if you make any mistake, but you get promoted to a better position and no longer have to close the shop after surviving 7 consecutive days. 

Unfortunately, we still face bugs that we need to patch, some of which are so interesting that I decided to share them with you:

https://i.imgur.com/5r5hmbM.gif

Currently, it is possible to squeeze through walls using a shopping cart, our character may have some supernatural powers, but this is unlikely to be one of them.

https://i.imgur.com/HfEkgju.gif


This is a classic one - getting stuck between an object and a wall. We are sure that players will find plenty of bugs like that after release, but we want to catch the most obvious stuck places.

That's all for today, Stay Tuned!

https://i.imgur.com/TttxmOn.gif

notes.title: Devlog #8 - Products and brands
notes.content:
Hello again everyone!

Every game starts with a concept,

which must be expressed with a certain art style. In the modern game dev industry, you can see that even indie studios can produce beautiful games with thoughtful gameplay - look at Hades 2 and Balatro from this year's launches, for example! 

But still, those games were produced by relatively big teams either creator alone made the game himself, which gave him freedom in fine-tuning his creation.

We, on the other hand, are trying to create something in a limited time, with a team that previously worked in different technologies and engine, with limited resources. Great.

Fortunately, there are places for creators like us, where we can find art which accelerate our work! 

ASSET STORES...

...such as Unity or Unreal one. Our supermarket location is a perfect example of such a thing, where first day we had the almost perfect location for our game, which we began to tweak to fit our needs. We don’t have much 3D workforce, so assets from this pack were a handful. The whole atmosphere of the supermarket also fit our concept, so it needed only little changes to distinguish it from the base one.

We have started slow and easy, from changing 2D assets and textures around the supermarket.

https://i.imgur.com/XUKUnlM.jpeg

https://i.imgur.com/ay3rBU8.jpeg

https://i.imgur.com/74lj0CH.jpeg


Those are small changes that still can affect the overall reception of the level and we will continue to do that which Ill present to you with pleasure in future progress devlogs.

And remember doors from our previous devlog? One day it will work the way we want it to, but unfortunately, it is not that day yet.

https://i.imgur.com/req7sX2.gif

That's it for the day, thanks everyone and stay tuned for more content!

notes.title: Devlog #7 - Door stuck!
notes.content:
Hello gamers!

Doors have always been a challenge for game designers.

Our first approach to door design took place in Electrician Simulator, our previous project. Players cannot expect what will happen after interacting with doors unlike real life - Will it open outwards or inwards? Outwards would be perfect for every door because it is the easiest scenario. But what if doors are opened inwards of the player? Sometimes it will bump up the player and push him away, or mess up with the camera. Maybe we should play an animation of opening doors? What if the player stays too close for doors when closing them, should we push him, or should doors stop closing?

SO MANY QUESTIONS.

https://i.imgur.com/Jr1Fu5g.gif

In the Electrician Simulator, we casually approached this problem - Every door opened outwards from the player, it solved the problem of awkward camera movement or the player being pushed away. Here, we choose a similar approach, but we are building Before Exit on a different game engine than Electrician Simulator so… that brings a new set of problems we haven’t encountered before.

Getting stuck between walls and doors, or doors that open inwards no matter what is just the tip of the iceberg. But we are working hard to solve every problem ASAP!

https://i.imgur.com/KmXshpF.gif

We have already teased things on our X.com profile, but thanks to wonderful Unreal technology we are planning to add human characters to our game! We don’t have much experience with people, because it is really difficult to make them right and give them proper life, so they don't look like puppets. 

We have worked with animated people and rigged models in the past but never managed to do it right. In the Electrician Simulator, we lacked experience and decided that the game would play better without them, but the levels and world always felt kind of empty without them. Now, on a smaller scale, we can experiment and try with them!

https://i.imgur.com/cfzQB5I_d.webp?maxwidth=1520&fidelity=grand

Thats all for today, Stay Tuned!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45055880/61ecd2a98c26c0810219661a18f451ad48985751.png

notes.title: Devlog #4 - Looking at exit rules
notes.content:
Hello customers!

Before we begin today’s devlog, there is a quick look at our Main Menu!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45055880/e6f35bcb07c41cb39a68725e22052a63cb081c39.gif

Of course, it’s still mostly WIP since the scene behind Menus is not ready but we have begun work on this part of the game and wanted to share that.

Let’s focus on the job.

In our first devlog (you can read it here: https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2983730/view/4146206839075089789?l=english) we write about our inspiration for the game and ideas for the gameplay. Today we will talk about the first mechanics that are coming into the game and how it all slowly comes together. 

We want to build our game around scenarios that will take place before the player's eponymous exit from work. We won't present the player with a given scenario, he will have to figure out what needs to be done by contextualizing environmental clues like stains on the floor or scattered objects. Each completed scenario leads to the next one.

Today I want to show you the first simple mechanics that will allow us to build the mentioned scenarios. 

Daily routines.

Our first mechanic was fundamental - throwing out bottles and trash that was lying around the shop. We figured that disappearing items on contact with the trashcan isn’t saying enough so we gave it little feedback on when the item is correctly thrown out:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45055880/d4b3f82088735c093bb01829c8b885e4f22b2325.gif

Another mechanic we are working on is the responsive rendering of shopping carts into place. Customers like to leave them in very non-obvious places, so one of the player's tasks will be to put them back in place.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45055880/c2169780f42b486cc11150e6a7b3c948d0a85968.gif

The last thing I want to show today is playing with physics in order to create fun mechanics for restocking store shelves. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45055880/f7f2af281983972aa97977d5c28334177a6511b6.gif

Thats all for today, Stay Tuned!

notes.title: Devlog #3 - Why Supermarket?!
notes.content:
Hello shoppers!

In today's developer log, we want to look at our action site and what inspired us to choose it.

Super Duper Mart

I must admit, I’ve started researching this devlog by searching for “most famous games supermarkets” in the internet browser BUT even before that I knew that games historically speaking had some pretty epic grocery stores. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45055880/5beabd0f51aebec2c5be4590295af049585ef2ce.jpg

For me, one from the headline of this paragraph is the most memorable one. Till today I can recall excitement and fear going there at the beginning of my journey in Fallout 3, it was the great early game location that taught you how to act inside interiors, where you look for loot, and how to sneak and approach enemies. After leaving the Super Duper Market, not only did we have pockets full of loot, but we also felt more confident in the Capital Wasteland.

But where was I?

Yes! A few things decided that the big grocery store would act as our playground:

Visual looks, aesthetics, atmosphere - We all love liminal, raw, and concerning spaces. Supermarkets are usually places where you autonomously meet other people, even if you don’t want to. People are subconsciously connected to this place, and removing them makes the location feel distressing, but also exciting. In Before Exit player is placed in the Supermarket after closing, where we want to express exactly those feelings.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45055880/968e769c1b7697cc39a8ab94a0a0bf359c9ce242.jpg

Plenty options of for fun mechanics! - Can you imagine being locked inside a supermarket all night and doing whatever you want? That would be terrifying… but also fun! There are carts to ride, fruits to throw, and products to try - there is really big potential in this playground!

Recent video game trends - Yeah, this is also a solid factor. Recently there was a popular game based in a similar place, it kinda inspired us. Fortunately, there is already another game about bananas that took the most popular spot so that puts us in an obsolete place.

That's all for today. It is worth mentioning that we are also active on X.com: https://x.com/beforeexitgame There you will find more content about our game, feel free to watch.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45055880/5a383da80097550e5a492074dfb3878910230051.png

notes.title: Devlog #2 - Everyone Out, now!
notes.content:
Hello customers,

Today we want to give you some glimpse on what was on our minds when coming with design of “Before Exit” and present more upcoming content!

Everyone Out, now!

As a studio, we are working fully stationary, directly from the office. Our working hours are very flexible, so when it comes to closing the office, there is no permanent person who holds this duty. Our place is always closed by the last person to leave. That forced us to prepare a special procedure of “closing the office”, where the last person has to check if every device is switched off, windows are properly closed, the water dispenser is disconnected from the socket and so on. Of course, no one is getting fired for forgetting one or two things, but BETTER REMEMBER TO DO THAT!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45055880/22febb32ff72a7e93c2be38e57c374ff5f524e28.jpg

That idea gave a spark to the prototype of the game that you all see today. It just felt like a basic gameplay loop - after all the hard work of the day there is only one last checklist to complete, and “That’s it!”. But did you remember about closing up the window in the conference room? Or turn the keyhole of the door? Those are feelings that come back to you every time, and I’m sure that you all know how it feels. I bet every one of you who read this has had to go back to their front door at least once to make sure it's locked properly!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45055880/c927698bcb51760bfcd6810b44afee8203249aae.jpg

So that’s the feeling we want to replicate in our game, this uncertainty when leaving the location. Fear of consequences. Relief when all went well.

You'll check if we succeeded soon!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45055880/5a383da80097550e5a492074dfb3878910230051.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45055880/1aad4c80bd57e63dca3b03d95b2f268cd13d2bef.png

notes.title: Devlog #1 - Hello… Boss?
notes.content:
Hello… Boss?

https://i.imgur.com/TrJa2l8.png

Surely you have once visited a supermarket moments before it closes, in need of that one IMPORTANT thing. The employees already practically have to close the cash registers, clean the aisles, and clear the floors, but you still haven't decided whether you prefer strawberry or vanilla yogurt! 

Their impatient gaze and firm tone are supposed to mobilize you to leave because after all, the last customer does not mean the end of their shift. Have you ever wondered what they do literally BEFORE they leave?

This is where our player's story begins.

Immediately after the last person leaves the store, at the behest of your strict supervisor, you are to make sure that everything is ready for its opening tomorrow, and any mistake could cost you your dismissal. 

Welcome Customers!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45055880/6ca05af7d9ffad9e07ebbda280d646fc6ce03a81.png

In Before Exit, you have been given the task of going out and closing the Supermarket as a new employee. Washing the floors, and correctly arranging the products on the shelves or expired yogurts are just some of your worries. Will you manage to keep your job?

We would like to present you our new production, an unusual arcade game with roguelike elements, where you will face seemingly routine activities in a humorous atmosphere. Put the game on your wishlist and follow our social profiles to stay up to date with it.
